title: The Roos differential of finite continuous bundles is epic
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P$ be profinite and $T$ a topological commutative ring. Let $R_T(Q\to P)=C(Q,T)$ on the finite jointly surjective site $\operatorname{Prof}/P$, as in [def-sfb-relative-finite-bundle-model]. Let $M:\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}$ be a tower, and for every $n\ge0$ let $E_n\to P$ be a finite locally constant abelian bundle with an additive section presentation of $M_n$, natural in every test over $P$, as defined there. Then the endomorphism $1-s$ of $\prod_n M_n$ is an epimorphism, where $(1-s)(x)_n=x_n-t_n(x_{n+1})$ and $t_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is the tower transition [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. No derived-category hypothesis, surjectivity of transitions, or uniform Mittag--Leffler bound is assumed.

proof.text: Form the total space of each bundle as the finite disjoint union of a clopen piece of P times its finite discrete group. Maps from a profinite test over P to this total space are exactly the sections in the given presentation: each coordinate section is locally constant and the finite clopen partition allows gluing. Naturality of the presentations conjugates a module transition to a natural transformation of these representable section functors. Evaluate it on the identity of the source total space to obtain a continuous map over P; naturality recovers the transformation by composition. Evaluation on pairs of sections gives fibrewise additivity.

Fix a test Q -> P and a product section y. Pull the bundles to Q. Their total spaces F_n are profinite finite unions of clopen products. In Q times the product of the F_n impose the closed equal-base conditions and the equations x_n-t_n(x_(n+1))=y_n(q). The equations are closed since the group operations and transition maps are continuous and the total spaces are Hausdorff. The ambient product is compact Hausdorff and has a clopen basis. Therefore the solution space Z_y is a closed profinite subspace with a continuous projection to Q.

For each q in Q the fibres are nonempty finite groups. Any finite family of equations is contained in an initial block through N. Set x_(N+1)=0, solve backwards x_n=y_n(q)+t_n(x_(n+1)) for n=N,...,0, and set all further coordinates to zero. Thus every finite family of closed equation sets has nonempty intersection in the compact product of the fibres. For the empty family the zero tuple supplies nonemptiness. The closed finite intersection theorem gives a solution to all equations. Hence Z_y -> Q is surjective; when Q is empty this is vacuous.

The single profinite surjection Z_y -> Q is an allowed cover. Coordinate sections give sections x_n on it through the given additive presentations. Sectionwise products assemble them into x, and the defining equations give (1-s)x=y restricted to Z_y. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf map is locally surjective and epic. Exact faithful forgetting reflects epimorphisms, proving the claim for module sheaves. Scalar compatibility is already supplied by the original tower morphisms, so no scalar choice or continuous global lifting is required.

theorem relativeFiniteBundle_roos_epi
    (P : Profinite.{u}) (T : Type v) [TopologicalSpace T] [CommRing T]
    [IsTopologicalRing T]
    (M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max u v + 1} (relativeContinuousRing P T))
    (E : ℕ → FiniteAbelianBundle P)
    (hE : ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((E n).SectionPresentation (M.obj (op n)))) :
    Epi (towerTransitionEndomorphism (K := fun n : ℕ ↦ M.obj (op n))
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ M.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op))
